investigation.root_cause: StorageService.setConnected() (storage.service.ts:44-50) stores the ApplinX Bearer session token in browser sessionStorage under key 'gx_token'. sessionStorage is accessible to all JavaScript code running in the same origin — any successful XSS can call sessionStorage.getItem('gx_token') to extract the token. Additionally, logger.service.ts:19 reads sessionStorage directly outside the StorageService abstraction, meaning the token is accessed in two places. No httpOnly cookie mechanism is used.
investigation.attack_scenario: Attack chain: VULN-001 (CSS injection) or VULN-002 (keyboard mapping eval) → JavaScript execution in app origin → sessionStorage.getItem('gx_token') → token exfiltration via fetch/XMLHttpRequest to attacker server → attacker uses token in Authorization: Bearer header → full ApplinX REST API access as victim. The attacker can read all terminal screen data, issue sendKeys commands, execute macros, and perform all operations the victim is authorized to do on the mainframe host.
prerequisites: User must be authenticated (token present in sessionStorage)
A prior XSS vulnerability (VULN-001, VULN-002, or any other XSS) must be exploitable
Session must be active (sessionStorage cleared on tab close)

privilege_boundary.start_privilege: Attacker with XSS execution in app origin (no session token)
privilege_boundary.achieved_privilege: Full authenticated ApplinX REST API session — all operations the victim user is authorized for on the host

impact.description: Full session hijack: attacker impersonates authenticated user to ApplinX REST API. Impact includes reading all terminal screen content (potentially including sensitive host data), issuing arbitrary host commands via sendKeys, executing/reading/deleting macros (including those with stored passwords, VULN-006), and full host session takeover for the duration of the token's validity.

sources: ApplinX REST API CreateSessionResponse.token — issued on successful authentication
transformations: sessionStorage.setItem('gx_token', authToken) — stored in JS-accessible storage
getAuthToken() returns 'Bearer ' + sessionStorage.getItem('gx_token') — used for all API calls and ngx-logger
sinks: sessionStorage['gx_token'] — accessible to all same-origin JavaScript
Authorization header of all ApplinX REST API calls
Authorization header of all ngx-logger remote log requests (VULN-012)

direct.impact: Direct sessionStorage access bypassing StorageService abstraction

indirect.impact: CSS injection attack chain pivot point — CSS-based exfiltration upgrades to token theft
Token also sent to remote logging endpoint — expanded attack surface

remediation_guidance.recommended_fix: Migrate to httpOnly/Secure cookie-based session token storage. This requires ApplinX REST API to support Set-Cookie response headers with HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict flags. The Angular client would remove all sessionStorage token handling — the cookie is transmitted automatically by the browser and inaccessible to JavaScript.
defense_in_depth: Migrate Bearer token to httpOnly/Secure cookie (requires backend change to ApplinX REST API)
If sessionStorage must be used: eliminate all non-StorageService sessionStorage token reads (fix logger.service.ts:19)
Implement CSP to restrict XSS vectors that could lead to token exfiltration
Implement short token lifetimes with automatic refresh to limit hijack window
Remediate XSS vectors (VULN-001, VULN-002) to eliminate the attack chain entry points
